people.name: Sris Chandra Basu
people.field: Sanskrit scholar, judge, writer and translator

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: Basu's father died leaving his mother to bring him up along with three other siblings including Baman Das Basu.

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: He was educated at the Lahore Mission School where his father had served as headmaster.

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: He received a scholarship to study at the Lahore Government College and passed the First Arts Examination with Arabic as his second language. He then continued studies for a BA degree... He passed his BA in 1881

relations.subject: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
relations.evidence: While in college, Sris Chandra took part in a Student's Rebellion, organizing a strike in protest against the principal Dr Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner for kicking a student.

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: Basu founded the Panini Office in November 1891 so as to publish his and other works.

relations.subject: Ramananda Chatterjee
relations.evidence: Ramananda Chatterjee, principal of the Kayastha Pathshala served as an editor.

relations.subject: Ramananda Chatterjee

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: He was a correspondent of Annie Besant and supported her cause for birth-control and translated some of her works.

relations.subject: Sris Chandra Basu
relations.evidence: Basu was titled Rai Bahadur in 1900 and nominated as a Fellow of the Allahabad University.
